title: Struggling with solo game dev project (what are workflows that work)
author: Embarrassed_Cap1673
selftext:
Been struggling with my dev project for years, started off using GMS, pivoted art style and mechanics and now trying to use Unity, but every time I get to the point of needing to customize new assets, I'm cooked. I've tried to use AI for a while now but don't have enough time to do the design work. I'm a developer but still need a bit of vision to develop my own assets.

Anyone have any ideas or has a proven workflow that actually works? Using blender and an ai tool end up being more work than making something low res from scratch...

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: The best workflow for AI gamedev is the workflow for gamedev, except you use some AI tools. So write a GDD, make lists of what you need, prototype, playtest, iterate.

comments.author: CaptainAlexWest
comments.body: It's game design document then prototype then show to social media then build the game out and ship it. It's the same progress as normal game dev but you have an ai super tool if you get stuck. You can go 10x speed.

comments.author: Embarrassed_Cap1673
comments.body: Issue is the assets, GDD, concept artechanics, game loop, all done, I just want to know how to make assets the easy way using ai

comments.author: DigitalDustChan
comments.body: There are a TON of asset packs on the asset store. Find one or a few that have the art style you like and buy them. AI can often fill in the holes if you need something slightly different but in the same style.

comments.author: count023
comments.body:
Yup, GDD is the way to go. 

Break your game into sections. Combat section, inventroy section, world/terrain section etc. 

Describe how each of them interact at a high level, then work on your game in modules.

I'm doing a 4x TBS game, i started simpy by making a global map, with the guts of the data structure, i can break that out into a UI management module, a sound module and a data handling module and document. When i move on to working on system/tile manipulatin, that module is self contained using th existing ui, data and sound and i only have to add in the extra module for handling the tile, etc... and work out that way.

IF you try to do it all in one, you will fail, you have to think, "what is self contained and what does it need to be aware of in other parts of the game", which is all you need to keep things self contained. Then when the linkages are needed, you capture that too, "this module needs access to the data module, or the ui module" and the can then bring in what it needs from other workflows at that time

comments.author: CordusPorf
comments.body: I used ai to write a game engine using C, Raylib and box 2d(probably more,  i don't know i didn't write it). I can simply export any blender scene and have a playable game, i can also use godot or Unity as the backend,  so my project exports to all three. Unreal with limited success because ai sizzle at blueprints.
